uncited: Ray-splat intersection algorithms evaluate the contribution of 3D Gaussians by intersecting viewing rays with the Gaussian primitives directly, rather than projecting them onto the image plane.
All methods in this family share the goal of computing the Gaussian's contribution $E$ along a ray $\mathbf{r}(t) = \mathbf{o} + t\mathbf{d}$.
This is the fundamental geometric operation shared by ray-based methods.
The concept of ray-Gaussian intersection originates from the need to accurately render 3D Gaussians without the approximations of affine projection.
